gold_decisions.identity_explanation: The gold issue concerns undefined endpoint evaluations and unsupported estimator theory for merely L2 forcing, including the missing spline or projected-data premise. ISSUE-002 concerns ill-typed reduced-basis norms and does not diagnose any forcing-data regularity or endpoint-evaluation defect.

The gold issue is the unjustified eigenfunction/eigenvalue framework for general coercive operators and infinite-dimensional spaces lacking self-adjointness or discrete spectrum. ISSUE-002 addresses a separate reduced-space norm typing problem and contains no diagnosis of the spectral assumptions.

Both entries diagnose the false uniform equivalence between right-endpoint evaluations of the quadratic modes and their element L2 or derivative norms. ISSUE-001 gives the vanishing endpoint counterexample and incompatible scaling, and its left-endpoint repair directly addresses the gold defect and its inf-sup consequences.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The claimed mesh- and eigenvalue-uniform right-endpoint control of quadratic invisible modes is false: endpoint values can vanish or have the wrong scaling while the element norms remain nonzero or grow, so the unrestricted inf-sup and related estimates are unsupported.

component_coverage.gold_component: The right-endpoint evaluation formula does not uniformly control the quadratic mode's element norms, with invisible modes defeating the positive inf-sup lower bound.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly supplies the zero-right-endpoint case at |T|lambda=3, shows nonzero element norms despite vanishing endpoint data, demonstrates nonuniform asymptotic scaling, and proposes left-endpoint control and corrected recursion. This independently diagnoses the complete false norm-equivalence and inf-sup failure.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both entries identify that the full solution and projection error are not reduced-space-valued, so taking their norms in the reduced Bochner-dual space is ill-defined. ISSUE-002 also identifies the failed cross-space dual-norm comparison and proposes an ambient or projection-based replacement, matching the gold repair.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The reduced-basis error theorem applies the reduced-space X_R norm to errors involving the full-space solution, even though those errors generally lie outside X_R; no ambient extension or valid full-to-reduced dual-norm control is supplied.

component_coverage.gold_component: The full-space solution errors are not elements of the reduced space, making the stated reduced-space norms and downstream bounds ill-formed without an ambient norm and corresponding control.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly distinguishes V_h from the proper reduced subspace, shows that both relevant errors lie outside X_R, explains why replacing the norm by X_h is not automatically valid, and proposes an ambient or projection-based error metric with the necessary stability relation.
